name: Galène
tagline: A light videoconference server in a single binary
description: A videoconference server and browser client designed for lectures, conferences and tutorials, and used for ordinary meetings too. It is one Go program with a built-in TURN server, and runs comfortably in 512 MB of memory.
backing: Written and maintained mainly by Juliusz Chroboczek, funded by NLnet's NGI0 Core programme and previously by Nexedi

maturity.rationale: Released since 2020, reached 1.0 in 2025 and ships several releases a year. It has run lectures at Université Paris Cité and Sorbonne Université and has had an NLnet-funded security audit. Development rests largely on one person and on grant funding.

selfHosting.summary: One binary, a data directory and a systemd unit. It needs a public IP rather than NAT, a real TLS certificate (it falls back to a self-signed one), and open UDP ports; most connection trouble comes from the ICE and TURN settings. Docker is possible but not recommended.

requirements.notes: Meetings cost CPU in proportion to the square of the participants: about 20 people on camera per core, 40 on four cores. Lectures scale much further, to about 300 listeners per core.

strengths: Very light: one binary, a few hundred megabytes of memory, a Raspberry Pi 5 will do
Guests join from a browser with an invitation link, no account needed
Server-side recording built in, with no extra component to run
Handles hundreds of listeners on a single core for lectures and talks
weaknesses: No shared whiteboard, and breakout rooms are a simpler subgroup mechanism
No end-to-end encryption for audio and video: the server must be trusted
No iOS app, and no screen sharing from mobile browsers
Meetings where everyone is on camera stop scaling at a few dozen people
A smaller project, essentially one maintainer, with no hosted offering and no Docker image to fall back on

featureNotes.guest-join: Through invitation links or public groups
featureNotes.large-meetings: Yes for lectures; meetings with everyone on camera top out at a few dozen
featureNotes.mobile-apps: Mobile browsers, and an Android app with chat, audio and screen sharing
